trace.code: default: return LITERAL;   // raw 0x00 is classified as a literal char (fix adds case '\0': return INVALID)
tokenadd(p, ch) appends the NUL into tokenbuf together with the following digits
p->tokenbuf[p->tokenpos] = 0;   // buffer read back as a C string: bytes after the embedded NUL are invisible
jv_number_with_literal(p->tokenbuf)   // "100\0" + "999" parses as 100, no 'Invalid numeric literal'
check_literal() returns success and tokenpos is reset, so the trailing digits are silently dropped
FIX (fbee8f4): case '\0': return INVALID;  -> 'Invalid character at line 1, column 3' for 12\0003

preconditions: the victim consumes attacker-influenced JSON through jq (shell/CI/automation gate, e.g. jq -e '.amount <= 100')
a second consumer of the same raw bytes tolerates or strips NUL characters (tr -d '\0', iconv, an ETL/text loader, a C-string reader)
the payload uses a raw 0x00 byte inside a numeric token; JSON-escaped \u0000 inside strings is correctly rejected

evidence.vulnerable_version: jq 1.8.2 (latest release, 2026-06-20); bug is long-standing (upstream regression test cites issue #3110)
evidence.fixed_version: master @ fbee8f48 (2026-08-23, PR #3606 'Reject raw NUL bytes in the parser instead of silently truncating tokens') -- NOT yet in any release
evidence.observed_result: Against the official jq 1.8.2 static Linux amd64 binary (SHA-256 b1c22172dd303f3be49e935aa56aa48a8b7a46e0bc838b4997d3bb451495870f): printf '100\000999' | ./jq-1.8.2 . prints 100 and exits 0 (no parse error), and {"amount":100\000999} yields .amount == 100 with exit 0. The modelled gate 'jq -e .amount <= 100' exits 0 (APPROVED) while the NUL-stripped ledger import of the same bytes reads amount 100999 -- a 100x over-limit record passes the jq gate. Control: the upstream fix's rule (classify(NUL) -> INVALID) reports 'Invalid character' for the same bytes, and the well-formed negative control {"amount":100} agrees (jq=100, ledger=100). Marker: JQMIMIC-CONFIRMED.

real_exploit.target: jq 1.8.2 released binary, JSON scanner src/jv_parse.c classify()/check_literal(); the bundled official jq-linux-amd64 build is executed directly on the crafted bytes
real_exploit.backend: official jq 1.8.2 static Linux amd64 release binary (bundled, SHA-256 pinned) + a modelled two-stage victim pipeline (jq gate + NUL-tolerant ledger import)
real_exploit.demonstrated: The real released jq accepts RFC 8259-invalid JSON containing a raw NUL inside a numeric token and silently truncates it (100\000999 -> 100, exit 0), while a NUL-stripping consumer of the same bytes reads 100999; a jq-based limit gate therefore approves an over-limit value. The fixed classify() rule rejects the same bytes with 'Invalid character'. CWE-436 interpretation conflict / CWE-170 improper NUL termination.

evidence.notes: Honest impact: this is a parser-differential / input-validation bug, not memory corruption. jq alone loses data silently (the trailing bytes never reach the output), but a real integrity impact requires the documented second consumer that tolerates NULs; hence AC:H and LOW severity. Raw NULs inside JSON strings are already rejected by jq's control-character check -- only numeric literals traverse the NUL-terminated check_literal() path. Fixed only on master (fbee8f4, 2026-08-23); latest release 1.8.2 predates it, so every released jq is affected.
